D-dimer_YEARS_model.recommendation: D-dimer cut-off levels adapted to clinical probability per the YEARS model (signs of DVT, haemoptysis, and whether an alternative diagnosis is less likely than PE).
criteria: PE excluded in patients without clinical items and D-dimer < 1000 µg/L
PE excluded in patients with one or more clinical items and D-dimer < 500 µg/L
D-dimer_YEARS_model.note: Low level of recommendation due to limitations (see Table 5).

Computed_tomography_venography_(4.12).summary: When using CTPA it is possible to image deep veins of the legs during the same acquisition.
limitations: Added value of venous imaging is limited

Assessment_of_pulmonary_embolism_severit.overall_message: Risk stratification of patients with acute PE is mandatory to determine appropriate therapeutic management.
Assessment_of_pulmonary_embolism_severit.initial_stratification: Based on clinical symptoms and signs of haemodynamic instability (high risk of early death).
Assessment_of_pulmonary_embolism_severit.advanced_stratification: For haemodynamically stable patients, assess (i) clinical, imaging and laboratory indicators of PE severity—mostly related to presence of right ventricular (RV) dysfunction—and (ii) presence of comorbidity or other aggravating conditions.

Clinical_parameters_of_PE_severity_(5.1).acute_RV_failure_definition: Rapidly progressive syndrome with systemic congestion resulting from impaired RV filling and/or reduced RV flow output; a critical determinant of outcome in acute PE.
Clinical_parameters_of_PE_severity_(5.1).prognostic_implication: These findings, alone or in combination, are associated with unfavourable short-term prognosis in acute PE.

Imaging_of_right_ventricular_size_and_fu.summary: Echocardiographic parameters are used to stratify early risk in PE; prognostic values summarized in supplementary materials.
